text: The applicant was born in 1961.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant lives in Surgut, Khanty-Mansiyskiy Region, Russia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was the leader of a trade union in a private company.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant's co-workers expressed a wish to hold a public assembly on Constitution Day on 12 December 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant, in his capacity as trade union leader, decided to help his co-workers hold a public assembly on Constitution Day on 12 December 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, his help to his co-workers was 'an indirect expression of his own opinion'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant distributed banners to his co-workers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant explained to his co-workers that it would be more practicable to stage solo demonstrations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: To avoid prosecution for holding a public assembly without notifying the authorities in advance, the applicant suggested that his co-workers position themselves at some distance from each other, for instance on different streets.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At the time of the events on 12 December 2009, there was no federal or regional statutory requirement concerning the minimum distance between simultaneous solo demonstrations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was arrested.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was taken to the police station after his arrest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was held at the police station for three hours.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 18 December 2009, a justice of the peace found the applicant guilty under Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace fined the applicant 1,500 Russian roubles (approximately 35 euros at the time).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace considered that the applicant and his co-workers had met in one place.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace considered that the applicant had given instructions to his co-workers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace considered that the applicant had distributed banners to his co-workers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace considered that the applicant had taken his co-workers to the place of the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace found that the above circumstances disclosed the presence of a group event in the form of a static demonstration (a 'picket').
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace found that the above circumstances confirmed the applicant's role as organiser of the group event.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace found that it was incumbent on the applicant to lodge a prior notification about the event to the competent authority as required by section 7 of the Public Events Act.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant appealed against the judgment of the justice of the peace of 18 December 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant noted that the Public Events Act defined a 'picket' as a form of public expression of opinion where one or more citizens with placards, banners and other means of visual expression stationed themselves near the target object of the 'picket'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant argued that there had been a separate 'target object' for each solo demonstrator.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant argued that the demonstrators had been positioned at a considerable distance from each other, for instance thirty metres apart for two of them.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant argued that he could not be lawfully considered as an organiser of a group event.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 22 January 2010, the Surgut Town Court upheld the judgment of the justice of the peace of 18 December 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: A summary of domestic law and practice concerning regulations relating to public events in Russia is contained in Novikova and Others v. Russia, application nos. 25501/07, 57569/11, 80153/12, 5790/13 and 35015/13, §§ 47-85, judgment of 26 April 2016.
